history.summary: CSV town corrected: the temple is at Hooli village, ~9 km from Saundatti in Belagavi district, not in Belgaum city. Hooli is one of the oldest villages in the Belgaum region; Wikipedia notes that most of its temples feature Chalukya architecture and were originally Jain bastis (basadis), and the village name is a corruption of PooValli ('flowery ear ornament'), also called Mahishpatinagar in ancient times. The Panchalingeshwara temple (five lingas) is an ASI-protected monument with fine Chalukya stone architecture, opposite the more modern Hari Mandir. The exact construction date of this temple was not established from available sources. Not to be confused with the Hoysala-era Panchalingeshwara Temple at Govindanahalli (Mandya district). Coordinates are for Hooli village (Wikipedia) - temple-level coordinates not found.

name: Hooli Panchalingeshwara Temple
town_description: Hooli is a historic village in Belagavi district, Karnataka, about 9 km from Saundatti. One of the oldest villages in the region, it has a rich temple heritage - most of its temples show Chalukya architecture and were originally Jain bastis - plus a ruined fort atop a nearby hill. The village has been ruled by the Rattas of Saundatti and the Patwardhans of Ramdurg. Its name is said to derive from PooValli, meaning a flowery ear ornament, and it was anciently known as Mahishpatinagar.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaivism) (temples of Hooli were originally Jain bastis)
